title: Mordecai Rises to the Top
overview: This short closing chapter sums up the king's power and Mordecai's rise to second in the empire, where he used his position for the good of his people.

parts.label: The king's wide reach (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The king imposed a tax, called tribute, across his whole empire, as far as its distant coasts and islands. For the rest of his deeds and Mordecai's rise, the writer points to the official royal records of Media and Persia, which have not survived.

parts.label: Mordecai's greatness (v. 3)
parts.note: Mordecai once sat at the palace gate. Now he ranks just below the king, is respected rather than resented by his own people, and uses his power to work for the good and safety of all the Jews.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether this ending mainly shows God quietly arranging Mordecai's rise, even though the book never mentions God, or mainly honors human courage and loyalty in a dangerous world.
think: What do you think it looks like for someone with real power to use it mostly for others rather than for themselves?
